title: Affine-space comparison
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], put
$\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $r\geq0$, let $X_r=\mathbf A^r_Y$,
$p_r:X_r\to Y$, with $X_0=Y$ and $p_0=\mathrm{id}_Y$, using
[def-sbc-affine-space]. Fix the standard coordinate order and identify
$X_{r+1}=\mathbf A^1_{X_r}$, with last-coordinate projection
$q_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$, so $p_{r+1}=p_rq_r$.
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Use the finite-level derived pullback and tensor
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the Tate twists
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the constructible exceptional
inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

Here is the precise ordered-composite definition. For every scheme $T$
here use the category $\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(T,A)$ of
[def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]: a bounded-below pro-etale complex
together with an etale complex and an isomorphism from its comparison
pullback. Bounded constructible complexes admit such witnesses by
[lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). On an affine chart the
projections above correspond to finitely generated polynomial algebras;
their diagonals are cut out by the differences of the coordinates.
Thus the projections are separated finite type and every $X_r$ is
separated finite type over $k$.

Apply [thm-sf-comp-composition] with $f=q_r$, $g=p_r$ and $S=Y$ to obtain
$$
 \alpha_r:Rp_{r!}Rq_{r!}\xrightarrow{\sim}R(p_rq_r)_!
$$
on $\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{r+1},A)$; the same theorem says that
these compact-support functors preserve the bounded-below etale-origin
class. Use its restriction to bounded constructible source complexes,
with the witnesses just specified. This restriction does not depend on
the choice of witness: the identity of the underlying complex is a
morphism between any two such witnessed objects by
[def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], and naturality of $\alpha_r$ identifies
the underlying components.
The constructible exceptional functors of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] have the adjunctions supplied by
[thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2), applicable to these bounded-below
etale-origin inputs. Let
$$
 c_r:R(p_rq_r)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_r^!Rp_r^!
$$
be the conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of this restricted
$\alpha_r$, using the composite adjunction with pasted unit and counit
of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2). Conjugation takes this isomorphism to
an isomorphism with the displayed reversed direction. The identity and
associativity clauses of [thm-sf-comp-composition], with conjugation and
mate pasting, fix the corresponding conventions for $c_r$.

Use the canonical finite Tate-line pullback identification as follows.
For each scheme $T$ here let $\nu_T$ be its site-comparison morphism
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Choose $a\geq1$ with $\ell^a A=0$
and put $B_{a,T}=\mu_{\ell^a,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^a}A$.
Use the projection-induced identification
$A_T(1)\cong\nu_T^*B_{a,T}$ in [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map],
independent of $a$. Here that node is applied to the empty effective
Cartier divisor, whose ideal is generated by the nonzerodivisor $1$.
The roots-of-unity sheaf is locally free of rank one over $\mathbf Z/\ell^a$
by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], applied first with coefficient
ring $\mathbf Z/\ell^a$; hence its ordinary tensor with $A$ equals its
derived tensor with $A$. Thus $B_{a,T}$ is locally free of rank one over the constant etale
$A$-sheaf: tensor an etale-local basis of $\mu_{\ell^a,T}^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $A$.
Pulling this basis to the pro-etale site shows that $A_T(1)$ is locally
free of rank one over $A_T$ as well, so its ordinary tensor powers compute
its derived tensor powers. For each projection $f:T'\to T$ use the composite
$$
 Lf^*A_T(1)\cong f_{\mathrm{proet}}^{-1}\nu_T^*B_{a,T}
 \cong\nu_{T'}^*f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}B_{a,T}
 \cong\nu_{T'}^*B_{a,T'}\cong A_{T'}(1).
$$
The middle two arrows are respectively the inverse comparison of
[lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the inverse-image identification
of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For $M\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$,
$r\geq0$ and $s\in\mathbf Z$, apply the finite-level ambient tensor
comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] to $M$ and the
finite Tate-line tensor power $A_T(1)^{\otimes r}$; the lemma applies to
arbitrary ambient inputs. Its
associativity, unit, and composition compatibilities, together with the
tensor-power associators, identify $Lf^*(M(r)[s])$ with
$(Lf^*M)(r)[s]$.
Twist additivity for the nonnegative integers used here is the
rebracketing $A(1)^{\otimes r}\otimes A(1)\cong A(1)^{\otimes(r+1)}$
from the definition of tensor powers; shifts add by $2r+2=2(r+1)$.
At finite coefficients the derived pullbacks are exact inverse images
applied termwise, as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; their
composition identification and the preceding tensor identifications fix
$$
 I_{r,K}:Lp_{r+1}^*K(r+1)[2r+2]
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 Lq_r^*\bigl(Lp_r^*K(r)[2r]\bigr)(1)[2].
$$
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, set $\gamma_{p_0,K}=\mathrm{id}_K$ and define
recursively
$$
 \gamma_{p_{r+1},K}
 :=c_r(K)^{-1}\circ\gamma_{q_r,Rp_r^!K}\circ
       \bigl(Lq_r^*(\gamma_{p_r,K})(1)[2]\bigr)\circ I_{r,K}.
$$
Here $\gamma_{q_r,-}$ is the affine-line comparison of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. Its input is in its stated
domain because [thm-sf-preservation-class] gives
$Rp_r^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_r,A)$ for these separated finite-type
projections. Thus the affine-space comparison is the specified map
$$
 \gamma_{p_d,K}:Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rp_d^!K
 \qquad(d\geq0),
$$
with the identity for $d=0$. No isomorphy of this map is included in
this definition; that is the affine-space purity assertion.

split_report.summary: Revalidated the complete construction against the current DAG after the landing refusal for thm-sf-comp-composition. Made its exact finite-coefficient, bounded-below etale-origin domain explicit; specialized it with f=q_r and g=p_r; restricted it to witnessed bounded constructible source complexes and explained independence from the witness. Cited the existing constructible-origin and relative-adjunction theorems before forming the conjugate c_r, with its correct direction and pasted adjunction. Rechecked every other current construction dependency, the finite Tate-line identifications, all four recursion arrows, and the master unit Step 6. Kept the reported base-scheme typing correction and finite-coefficient binding, and created no new nodes. No Lean was written or compiled.
split_report.blueprint: The imported definition and sk-prop-an Step 6: gamma_{p_{r+1},K}=c_r^{-1} gamma_{q_r,Rp_r^!K} Lq_r^*(gamma_{p_r,K})(1)[2], with the source rebracketing I_{r,K} explicit; gamma_{p_0,K}=id. No statement of coordinate symmetry or purity is folded into the definition.

tool_uses.why: Its current statement supplies alpha_{p_r,q_r} on bounded-below witnessed etale-origin complexes; restriction to bounded constructible source objects is conjugated to c_r in the unit Step 6 recursion.
Pasted composite adjunctions and the mate-pasting identities fix the coherence of c_r; this is a categorical tool for the composition datum.
Only the stated etale-origin witness and projection-induced identification of the finite Tate line are used; no Cartier purity conclusion is used.
Pullback of the finite etale Tate-line witness supplies the pro-etale comparison after the existing site comparison; this does not replace a purity step.
The coherent etale/pro-etale inverse-image comparison transports the finite Tate-line pullback map, without identifying coefficient categories silently.
The derived tensor comparison turns the Tate-line pullback identification into the twist identification required to type I_r.
Only finite-stage finite-Tor preservation types the input Rp_r^!K to the already defined affine-line comparison; no affine-space isomorphy is inferred.

Clause (ii) supplies etale-origin witnesses for bounded constructible source complexes, exactly the domain required by the current compact-support composition theorem; this types the unit compositor and changes no purity route.

Clause (2) supplies the relative exceptional adjunction on the same bounded-below etale-origin source class, needed to conjugate the compact-support compositor; the unit does not reconstruct these general adjunctions.

lean.note: Ordered recursion with literal dimension-zero identity.
